title: Saying What You Want: querer, tomar, comer

sections.title: Ordering food and drink
sections.content: Use 'querer' (to want) to say what you'd like. It changes its stem from e to ie in most forms: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren. 'Tomar' (to have a drink, to take) and 'comer' (to eat) are regular -ar and -er verbs, so they follow the normal pattern: tomo/tomas/toma, como/comes/come.

items.english: Do you want to have a coffee?
I also want to eat something.
What would you like? (asked by a waiter to more than one person)

sections.content: 'Querer' is one of the most common stem-changing verbs in Spanish — the e becomes ie everywhere except nosotros/vosotros. You'll meet more verbs that follow this same pattern later on.
